blocks.source: 【作曲講座】編曲する
blocks.translation: [Composition Guide] Arranging

blocks.source: 曲は一応の完成をみたもののどうも物足りない。そんな時でも後から編曲することによって、よくすることができます。色んな編曲方法を紹介してみます。
blocks.translation: Even after a song is technically finished, it can still feel like something is missing. Even then, you can improve it by arranging it afterward. Here are several arranging methods.

blocks.source: 別に以下の全てをやる必要はありません。手を加えればいいというものでもないので、よさげなものだけでＯＫです。
blocks.translation: You don't need to do everything below. Adding more isn't necessarily better, so just use whatever seems useful.

blocks.source: 主旋律
blocks.translation: Main Melody

blocks.source: 付点音符
blocks.translation: Dotted Notes

blocks.source: 初心者にありがちなのは『２分音符』『４分音符』『８分音符』などで曲を構成してしまいがちなこと。『付点２分音符』『付点４分音符』『付点８分音符』なども積極的に使ってみましょう。
blocks.translation: Beginners often tend to compose songs using only notes such as half notes, quarter notes, and eighth notes. Try actively using dotted half notes, dotted quarter notes, and dotted eighth notes as well.

blocks.source: 僕の場合『付点８分音符→付点８分音符→８分音符』の構成は使い勝手がよいので、よく使っています。（上の赤枠が例）戦闘曲で多用するとどことなくイトケンっぽい。
blocks.translation: In my case, I often use the pattern “dotted eighth note → dotted eighth note → eighth note” because it is easy to work with. (The red box above is an example.) Using it frequently in battle music gives it a somewhat ItoKen-like feel.

blocks.source: 伴奏
blocks.translation: Accompaniment

blocks.source: １／２小節単位にしてみる
blocks.translation: Try Using Half-Measure Units

blocks.source: 別に一小節単位でコード進行を作らねばならないわけでもありません。１／２小節単位にしてみましょう。
blocks.translation: You don't necessarily have to create chord progressions one measure at a time. Try using half-measure units.

blocks.source: 上ではサビの伴奏を１／２小節単位に変更してみました。
blocks.translation: Above, I changed the accompaniment for the chorus to half-measure units.

blocks.source: ベースを伴奏に沿わせる場合はそちらも変更が必要です。
blocks.translation: If you want the bass to follow the accompaniment, you will need to change it as well.

blocks.source: もう少し複雑に
blocks.translation: Make It a Little More Complex

blocks.source: 冒頭部分です。１６分音符を使って細かく刻んでみました。ノリがよい感じになります。
blocks.translation: This is the opening section. I used sixteenth notes to create finer subdivisions. It gives the song a more energetic feel.

blocks.source: 楽器を変える
blocks.translation: Change the Instruments

blocks.source: 伴奏にはピアノやギターなども使用できます。色々と試してみてください。
blocks.translation: You can also use instruments such as piano and guitar for the accompaniment. Try experimenting with different options.

blocks.source: ベース＆リズム
blocks.translation: Bass & Rhythm

blocks.source: もう少し複雑に
blocks.translation: Make It a Little More Complex

blocks.source: ベース
blocks.translation: Bass

blocks.source: サビのベースです。元々は適当に８分音符を並べただけでした。今度は１６分音符に変更してみます。
blocks.translation: This is the bass for the chorus. Originally, I had simply lined up eighth notes at random. This time, I'll change them to sixteenth notes.

blocks.source: リズム
blocks.translation: Rhythm

blocks.source: 冒頭のリズムです。ベースと合わせてリズムを変えてみました。
blocks.translation: This is the rhythm for the opening. I changed the rhythm to match the bass.

blocks.source: 曲の変わり目に変化をつける
blocks.translation: Add Variation at Section Changes

blocks.source: 例えば４小節目や８小節目といった区切りのリズムやベースを変化させます。すると曲の代わり目がはっきりしてメリハリが付きます。
blocks.translation: For example, change the rhythm or bass at transitional points such as the fourth or eighth measure. This makes the transitions between sections clearer and adds contrast.

blocks.source: 上はサビの８小節目です。
blocks.translation: The above is the eighth measure of the chorus.

blocks.source: 楽器を変える
blocks.translation: Change the Instruments

blocks.source: 例えば、ベースの楽器を代わりにピチカート（046:Pizzicato）にしてみます。クロノトリガーの中世で流れるアレですね。久石譲でもよいですが。町の曲などにも有用です。
blocks.translation: For example, try replacing the bass instrument with pizzicato (046:Pizzicato). You know, that familiar sound heard in the medieval era of Chrono Trigger. Joe Hisaishi would work too. It is also useful for town themes.

blocks.source: ゆったりした曲調なら、低音部はベースではなくバイオリンやストリングス、ギターなどに任せてもよい感じです。
blocks.translation: For a slower song, the low-register part can be handled by violin, strings, or guitar instead of bass.

blocks.source: 他のパートも追加
blocks.translation: Add More Parts

blocks.source: ハープ
blocks.translation: Harp

blocks.source: 定番のハープ（047:Harp）をサビに追加してみます。ＦＦのフィールドなどでもおなじみですが、これでいかにもＲＰＧのフィールド曲といった感じになりました。
blocks.translation: Let's add the classic harp (047:Harp) to the chorus. It is also familiar from the fields in Final Fantasy, and it gives the song a distinctly RPG field-theme feel.

blocks.source: 激しく上下する音符を見ると、急にややこしくなったように見えますが、コード進行に沿って上下しているだけです。「ミソドミソドミソ」「ドソミドソミドソ」というように機械的にやっているだけなので怖気づく必要はありません。
blocks.translation: The notes moving sharply up and down may make the part suddenly look complicated, but they are simply moving up and down along with the chord progression. It is just a mechanical pattern such as “E-G-C-E-G-C-E-G” or “C-G-E-C-G-E-C-G,” so there is no need to be intimidated.

blocks.source: 何となく４小節目だけ変えてみましたが、どうするかはお好みで。１６分音符ではなく、８分音符にするとゆったりした感じになります。
blocks.translation: I changed only the fourth measure somewhat arbitrarily, but what you do is up to you. Using eighth notes instead of sixteenth notes gives it a more relaxed feel.

blocks.source: 副旋律（ハモり）を追加
blocks.translation: Add a Secondary Melody (Harmony)

blocks.source: 別のメロディを追加してハモらせましょう。楽器はわりと自由に選べると思います。普通は音量と合わせて、主旋律より目立たないように抑えます。
blocks.translation: Add another melody and harmonize it. You can choose the instrument fairly freely. Normally, lower its volume along with other adjustments so that it does not stand out more than the main melody.

blocks.source: なお、ハモりは必ずしも全ての小節に追加する必要はありません。部分的に使用したほうが効果的なことも多いです。上では冒頭の２ループ目だけに追加してみました。
blocks.translation: The harmony does not necessarily need to be added to every measure. It is often more effective when used only in certain sections. Above, I added it only to the second loop of the opening.

blocks.source: 可能なら主旋律とは、ある程度音の高さをズラしたほうが聞き取りやすくなります。あんまり高音域や低音域で鳴らされても聞き苦しかったりしますけどね。
blocks.translation: If possible, shifting the pitch of the harmony to some degree from the main melody makes it easier to hear. That said, having it play too high or too low can also make it unpleasant to listen to.

blocks.source: もちろん目立つ不協和音にならないように注意しなくてはなりません。かといって、主旋律やコード進行と同じ音階を鳴らすだけでは面白みにかけます。
blocks.translation: Of course, be careful not to create conspicuous dissonance. On the other hand, simply playing the same scale as the main melody and chord progression makes it rather uninteresting.

blocks.source: そんなわけで比較的センスが要求される箇所だと思います。ここに挙げたテクの中では比較的難しめです。
blocks.translation: That makes this a section that requires a relatively good sense of musical judgment. Of the techniques introduced here, this is one of the more difficult ones.

blocks.source: 完成！
blocks.translation: Finished!

blocks.source: 上記の編曲を色々と反映してみました。今度こそ完成です！ 上に挙げた以外にも若干の微調整をしています。ちなみに作曲にかかったのは精々３時間程度。画面キャプチャーを取りながら、記事を書くほうがよほど労力がかかっています。
blocks.translation: I applied various elements of the arrangement described above. Now it is finally finished! I also made some minor adjustments beyond what I mentioned above. Incidentally, composing the song took only about three hours at most. Writing the article while taking screenshots required far more effort.

blocks.source: TestField_Arrange.mid
blocks.translation: TestField_Arrange.mid

blocks.source: ちょっと物足りないかもしれませんが、なるべくシンプルに、誰でもできそうな方法でやったのでご容赦ください。あくまで初心者向けです。これ以上を求める方は、音楽理論をきちんと学ぶなり、好きな曲を聴いたり、真似てみるなりで研鑽に励んでください。特に主旋律以外の部分を意識して聞くことが重要です。
blocks.translation: It may still feel a little lacking, but please forgive me—I used methods that were as simple as possible and that anyone could probably do. This is strictly intended for beginners. If you want to go further, work on improving your skills by properly studying music theory, listening to songs you like, and trying to imitate them. In particular, it is important to listen consciously to parts other than the main melody.

blocks.source: 音源を変えてみる
blocks.translation: Try Changing the Sound Source

blocks.source: もう一つ。どんなに良い曲を作っても音源がWindowsのデフォルトでは物足らない。そんな人は音源を導入することをオススメします。
blocks.translation: One more thing. No matter how good a song you make, it will feel lacking if the sound source is the Windows default. If that sounds like you, I recommend installing a different sound source.

blocks.source: 今時のゲーム音楽ではフリーゲームであっても、だんだんＭＩＤＩは使用されなくなってきています。音源で録音した曲を演奏する流れになっていくはずです。
blocks.translation: Even in today's game music, MIDI is gradually falling out of use, including in freeware games. The trend will likely shift toward playing songs recorded using sound sources.

blocks.source: 音源といっても色々とありますが、何をやるにしても敷居は高いです。フリーで使用できるものでは『サウンドフォント』と『TiMidity++』の組み合わせが比較的導入が簡単なのでオススメです。僕の場合、サウンドフォントを使用した音源を使い、Dominoで演奏しながら作曲しています。
blocks.translation: There are various types of sound sources, but whichever route you take, the barrier to entry is high. Among the options available for free, I recommend the combination of SoundFont and TiMidity++, as it is relatively easy to install. In my case, I compose while performing in Domino using a sound source based on SoundFont.

blocks.source: 例えば、こんな感じにできあがります。
blocks.translation: For example, you can end up with something like this.

blocks.source: TestField_Arrange_SF.mp3
blocks.translation: TestField_Arrange_SF.mp3

blocks.source: もっとも、サウンドフォントまでやり出すと収拾がつかなくなるので、これ以上はやりません。本当に凝りだすと際限がないので……。そのため、詳しくは『サウンドフォント』や『TiMidity++』でググってください。既に情報はたくさんあります。
blocks.translation: However, once you start getting into SoundFonts, things can quickly get out of hand, so I will not go any further. There is no end to it once you really get absorbed in it.... So, search Google for “SoundFont” and “TiMidity++” for more details. There is already plenty of information available.

blocks.source: 以上で、とりあえずの作曲講座は完成です。その内、フィールド曲だけではなく戦闘曲とかもやるかもしれません。……やらないかもしれません。
blocks.translation: That concludes this basic composition guide for now. At some point, I may cover not only field themes but also battle music. ...Or maybe I won't.
